previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with chronic idiopathic pancreatitis was readmitted the day after discharge due to recurrent severe epigastric pain, nausea, and constipation unrelieved by oral medications. She was managed with NPO status, IV fluids, and TPN restart. Pain was controlled with IV and transitioned to oral hydromorphone, with the fentanyl patch reduced to 100 mcg/hr. She tolerated oral medications for two days prior to discharge and required no IV medications in the final 24 hours. An MRCP showed stable chronic pancreatitis changes without new pathology. Constipation was managed with her home bowel regimen plus additional doses. She remained on her baseline psychiatric and GERD medications. No infectious source was found. She was discharged home with TPN, home health support, and follow-up arranged with her GI doctor and a new pain clinic consultation to address opioid dependence.

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  ___ woman with pancreatitis.  Assess for infiltrate.

COMPARISON:  Multiple prior chest radiographs, with the latest on ___.

PA AND LATERAL CHEST RADIOGRAPH:  The central catheter is again seen with the
tip terminating in the cavoatrial junction.  The lungs are clear without
pneumothorax, pleural effusions or focal airspace consolidations.  The
cardiomediastinal silhouette, hilar contours and pulmonary vasculature are
normal.  Mild-to-moderate thoracic kyphosis is unchanged.

IMPRESSION:  No acute cardiopulmonary process.  No pleural effusions.

INDICATION:  ___ woman with history of chronic pancreatitis and fungal
infection.  Has a tunneled line in place which needs to be removed and the tip
sent for culture.

CLINICIANS:  Dr. ___, Dr. ___, and Dr. ___
(attending). 

PROCEDURE:  The patient was brought down to the ___ section and placed in the
recovery unit.  A usual timeout and huddle was performed as per ___
protocol.  The skin around the area of the tunneled catheter was prepped and
draped in the usual sterile fashion.  1% lidocaine was used to anesthetize the
subcutaneous tract.  A few initial attempts to pull the catheter out were
unsuccessful.  We then used sharp dissection to separate the fibrous tissue
around the cuff.  The catheter was then pulled out easily in entirety.  The
tip was sent for culture.  Firm pressure was held on the venotomy site until
hemostasis was achieved.  No immediate complications were noted.

IMPRESSION:  Successful removal of right-sided tunneled line.The catheter tip
is sent for culture sensitivity.
